quests.question: She walked ___ the room and sat down.
quests.hint: 'Into' shows movement from outside to inside.
quests.explanation: 'Into' indicates movement from outside to inside an enclosed space. 'In' shows location, not movement.

quests.question: He poured the water ___ the glass.
quests.hint: 'Into' is used when liquid moves from one container to another.
quests.explanation: 'Into' describes movement into a container: pour water into a glass, drop coins into a jar.

quests.question: She stepped ___ the stage to collect her prize.
quests.hint: 'Onto' shows movement to the top of a surface.
quests.explanation: 'Onto' means movement to a position on top of something: step onto the stage, climb onto the roof.

quests.question: He jumped ___ the pool from the side.
quests.hint: 'Into' shows movement from outside the pool to inside it.
quests.explanation: 'Into' is used for movement into an enclosed space or body of water: jump into the pool, dive into the sea.

quests.question: She ran ___ the building to escape the rain.
quests.hint: 'Into' shows movement from outside to inside.
quests.explanation: 'Into' indicates movement through an entrance into an enclosed space: run into the building.

quests.question: The bird flew ___ of the cage.
quests.hint: 'Out of' shows movement from inside to outside.
quests.explanation: 'Out of' means movement from inside to outside: fly out of the cage, walk out of the room.

quests.question: She walked ___ the bridge slowly.
quests.hint: 'Across' means from one side to the other on a surface or bridge.
quests.explanation: 'Across' describes crossing from one side to the other: walk across the bridge, swim across the lake.

quests.question: He drove ___ the tunnel in about five minutes.
quests.hint: 'Through' means passing from one end to the other of a narrow space.
quests.explanation: 'Through' is used for enclosed or narrow spaces: drive through a tunnel, walk through a forest.

quests.question: They sailed ___ the island.
quests.hint: 'Around' means moving in a circuit surrounding something.
quests.explanation: 'Around' describes movement in a circuit or path surrounding something: sail around the island, walk around the lake.

quests.question: She climbed ___ the roof to fix the antenna.
quests.hint: 'Onto' shows movement to the top of something.
quests.explanation: 'Onto' indicates movement to the top surface: climb onto the roof. 'On the roof' describes the location after arrival.

quests.question: The cat jumped ___ the fence to the other side.
quests.hint: 'Over' means passing from one side to the other by going above.
quests.explanation: 'Over' is used when you go above something to cross it: jump over the fence, climb over the wall.

quests.question: He slid ___ the table and out the window.
quests.hint: 'Across' means moving along a surface from one side to the other.
quests.explanation: 'Across' is used for movement along a flat surface from one side to the other: slide across the table.

quests.question: She walked ___ the park on her way home.
quests.hint: 'Through' means passing within an area from one side to the other.
quests.explanation: 'Through' is used for passing within an area: walk through the park means you went inside it from one side to the other.

quests.question: They drove ___ the station without stopping.
quests.hint: 'Past' means going beyond a point without stopping.
quests.explanation: 'Past' indicates going beyond a reference point: drive past the station, walk past the shop.

quests.question: He ran ___ the street to catch the bus.
quests.hint: 'Across' - crossing a road goes from one side to the other.
quests.explanation: 'Across' is used when crossing from one side of something to the other: run across the street, look across the valley.

quests.question: She cycled ___ the river path for thirty minutes.
quests.hint: 'Along' means following the length of a path.
quests.explanation: 'Along' describes movement following the length of a path, road, or river: cycle along the path, walk along the beach.

quests.question: The plane flew ___ the mountains.
quests.hint: 'Over' shows movement passing above something.
quests.explanation: 'Over' describes movement above something while crossing it: fly over the mountains, jump over the fence.

quests.question: She moved ___ the sofa to make room.
quests.hint: 'Aside' or 'away' can work, but 'aside' best fits 'move aside'.
quests.explanation: 'Move aside' means to move to one side to make space. 'Move away' means to go to a different place entirely.

quests.question: He is moving ___ the city to work in the countryside.
quests.hint: 'Move away from' means leaving a place.
quests.explanation: 'Move away from' describes leaving a place: move away from the city means leaving city life behind.

quests.question: She is walking ___ the town centre to meet her friend.
quests.hint: 'Toward' (or 'towards') means in the direction of.
quests.explanation: 'Toward/towards' means moving in the direction of something: walk towards the centre.

quests.question: The children are running in and ___ of the garden.
quests.hint: 'In and out of' describes back-and-forth movement through a space.
quests.explanation: 'In and out of' describes repeated movement into and out of a space: running in and out of the garden.

quests.question: She reached ___ for the book on the top shelf.
quests.hint: 'Reach up' means to extend your arm upward.
quests.explanation: 'Reach up' describes extending upward: reach up for something high. 'Reach out' means to extend sideways.

quests.question: He turned ___ at the end of the road.
quests.hint: 'Turn around' means to change direction.
quests.explanation: 'Turn around' means to change direction and go back the way you came. 'Turn back' means to return.

quests.question: She bent ___ to pick up the pen from the floor.
quests.hint: 'Bend down' means to lower your body toward the floor.
quests.explanation: 'Bend down' describes lowering the body toward the floor to pick something up.

quests.question: They moved ___ a bigger house last year.
quests.hint: 'Move into' means starting to live in a new place.
quests.explanation: 'Move into' is used when you start living in a new home: move into a flat, move into a house.

quests.question: She took the book ___ the shelf.
quests.hint: 'Take off' a surface means to remove something from it.
quests.explanation: 'Take off' a shelf means to remove something from its surface. Compare 'take out of' a bag (from inside).

quests.question: He drove his car ___ the garage after work.
quests.hint: 'Drive into' a garage - movement from outside to inside.
quests.explanation: 'Into' is used for movement from outside to inside an enclosed space: drive into the garage.

quests.question: She fell ___ the stairs and hurt her ankle.
quests.hint: 'Fall down' the stairs means to tumble downward.
quests.explanation: 'Fall down the stairs' describes tumbling downward along the stairs. 'Fall off' means to fall from a surface.

quests.question: He picked up the bag and walked ___ the door.
quests.hint: 'Walk out of' means to exit through the door.
quests.explanation: 'Walk out of' means to exit: he walked out of the door. 'Walk out' without 'of' is also common informally.

quests.question: She squeezed ___ the narrow gap in the hedge.
quests.hint: 'Through' is used for narrow openings and spaces.
quests.explanation: 'Through' means passing within and out of a narrow space: squeeze through a gap, crawl through a tunnel.
